title: What do you guys think this holds for the future?
author: TuggerHuggerFugger
selftext: I was on the wagon aa well of AI hate. It felt very very powerful. People are generating tons of stuff. How do experienced coders feel about this? As a tool I'm sure you guys are estactic. But also as a tool that can use to create from a complete beginner, how do you guys see it? I do think it's cool, I wish Toby fox used it to push out his game faster.

comments.author: Lavio00
comments.body:
For vibecoders: The initial hype of creating actual games with AI will die out when they realize there’s a huge difference between a vertical slice and an actual game.

For devs: small studios will perform what larger studios can, and the cost/benefit of large studios will not be good.

… all of that is if we dont get new groundbreaking advances in upcoming models. If we do… well…

replies.author: TuggerHuggerFugger
replies.body: Interesting. What seemingly was companies trying to replace many, was a double edged sword because it allows smaller teams to create things on a bigger level now. Cool.

replies.author: orbital_trace
replies.body: We don't even need new models, just better mcps and tools for the models we currently have to interact with.

comments.author: Safe-Worldliness7321
comments.body: its fun the mess around with. speaking of deltarune it opens the door for a lot of people to make their own takes/AU's

comments.author: Fit_Enthusiasm4995
comments.body: seen a few 'complete' ai games that were just a loop of the same 3 dialogue choices. the real bottleneck isn't code, it's pacing and player agency. no amount of prompts fixes that.

replies.author: Valdaraak
replies.body: Basically. AI can make a game. It can't make a *good* game on its own. It's the human's job to provide all the details, plans, information, and oversight to make it good.

comments.author: PositiveScarcity8909
comments.body:
There is a huge gap between someone who knows coding and someone who doesn't in results even using the latest AI models.

Im a complete beginner with no idea about actual coding and I basically need to trust the AI completely so there are a ton of blind spots that come up later to bite you in the ass, especially in a real project.

Why do you think the current trend for AI games is tower defense and survivor games? It's because those are games with no assets, no animation, barely any dialogue and just based on numbers which is the AIs strong suit.

The rest of prototypes you see here are mostly one level prototypes that fall apart if you play for more than 10 minutes.

comments.author: Simtetik
comments.body:
Steam or Epic become the Spotify of gaming. You pay a subscription for unlimited access to every game in their system.

Developers/publishers are paid per unique subscription user that plays there game, similar to how Spotify currently pays artists/publishers.

The number of games available to play gets more and more overwhelming. But just like music, we will carve out our favourites and sometimes discover and indie gem to add to our rotation. 

The amount of money the average indie developer earns will be small. A side hustle for practically all but a few. The really good developers will find ways to make money besides the standard game royalties. They'll need their version of the "world tour" that currently gives massive income stream to popular musicians.

replies.author: SnoutUp
replies.body:
>The amount of money the average indie developer earns will be small.

Surprised to see this here, since very few want to think about it and prefer to keep the dream alive. In reality, we're all end up fighting for scraps. AI dev or no AI, the already hard publishing and competition is going get many times worse. I see quite a few "wait, where are my players?" threads popping up already.

And before someone comes out with "standout games will earn!", first of all, AI will make it so that fewer games will standout, big indie earners will be rarer and they will earn less, because others will rush to fill the niche or iterate on the idea.

comments.author: Valdaraak
comments.body:
>How do experienced coders feel about this? As a tool I'm sure you guys are estactic

Based on the ones I've interacted with, the answer is "it depends on who you ask."

Some are very glad they don't have to write code any longer and just need to review and test. These are typically the devs that became devs because it paid well and coding is a means to an end.

The devs who have a passion for coding and building things with their hands hate it to the point I'm convinced some of the ones I know are about to have a mental breakdown due to their job being "babysitting agents all day" and "the company literally has a rule that all code has to be AI." Those are the ones that have a hair trigger with AI and will go on huge, unprompted rants whenever you try to say there are valid uses for it, and they'll dismiss any evidence you give them.

comments.author: ModernGameDev
comments.body:
As someone who’s been coding for a lil over a decade I am ecstatic that AI can do most of the coding and I can learn and worry more about the game design from now on.

And I honestly don’t care what everyone else is doing (except cloning and reselling, that’s just wrong) I’m just glad I can make the games that’s been collecting dust in my notes for years now.

And beginner or experienced dev, coding isn’t the heart of game dev, it’s game design. I want everyone to make their imaginations a reality.

comments.author: CandidateDue2480
comments.body:
It won't change the % of people that actually finish a game compared to before. Games are hard, and the things that make games truly hard aren't really the things that AI solve.

I'm an indie dev working in well known AAs and yeah it massively enhances my capabilities, I can do things it would have taken a team of designers and programmers before.

But we'll also likely reduce our team size after next game launch as a result.

AAA is all using it en masse and it will definitely result in even more redundancies deep into next year as people automate out their jobs, or studio heads realize they can reduce headcount and automate people.

comments.author: LukPuk1
comments.body:
Using AI for personal project or in small team is big big difference than working in AAA, when 300 people is building project with AI spitting tons of code which people dont know much about as there is not much time to consolidate... huge tech-dept is built, which eventually kill the project.

I feel AI will make smaller teams more efficient, but break larger teams if not careful.

replies.author: Time_Cat_5212
replies.body:
Lmao I can only imagine how some big companies are just tripping over themselves to build these massive slopcanoes

So far I don't think we've hit the "less is more, use AI to build intentionally" phase yet. It all seems to be more more more go go go, bigger is better, yolo.

comments.author: SaltyVon
comments.body: Either games are going to become way cheaper because people can make their own, or studios will give out methods to facilitate personal indie games themselves and sell that instead of making games as much as they do.
